svg.text: Why a minority can never write, and why healing is truncate-and-replay rather than merge

g.text: the majority elects in a NEW term
the majority elects in a NEW term
heal: the stale tail is truncated
heal: the stale tail is truncated
Every decision - electing a leader, committing an entry - needs a majority, and majorities always overlap.
any two majorities of the same cluster share at least one node, and that node remembers the newer term
The leader ends up alone on one side. It does not know that yet - it only knows its acks stopped arriving.
in the e2e-ha suite this is a real Docker network disconnect, not a simulated one
A leader that cannot reach a majority cannot commit anything, so it gives up leadership by itself.
entries it had appended but not committed stay uncommitted - no client was ever told they succeeded
The two connected nodes hold a majority, so they can elect - and they do it in a higher term.
term 1 -> term 2; the old leader is still on term 1 and will be corrected the moment it is reachable again
Two acks out of three is still a majority, so the connected side keeps committing normally.
the cluster tolerates the loss of one node out of three - that is exactly what majority quorum buys
On the isolated side nothing can commit, so a write there fails or times out instead of diverging.
this is the whole point: a minority that cannot commit cannot produce a second, conflicting history
On rejoin the old leader sees the higher term, drops the entries it never committed and takes the leader's.
index 4 on the old leader was never acknowledged to any client, so discarding it loses nothing that was promised
Split-brain is not detected and repaired here - the algorithm makes a second history impossible to create.
one leader per term + majority overlap + commit-before-answer: a committed entry survives every later election
